title: Adult with acute chest pressure
opening: Hello. I have been having pressure in my chest and I am worried.

disclosures.response: It feels like pressure right in the middle of my chest. It started about 30 minutes ago.
It seems to move into my left arm, especially when the pressure gets worse.
I am a little short of breath, but I can still speak in full sentences.
I take a blood-pressure medicine. I have high blood pressure, but no known medication allergies.
I used to smoke, but I quit around five years ago.

metrics.name: Introduction and consent
metrics.rationale: Introduces self and establishes permission or rapport.
metrics.coaching_hint: Introduce yourself and ask permission: 'Hi, I'm [your name]. Is it okay if I ask a few questions?'

metrics.name: Symptom characterization
metrics.rationale: Explores onset, location, character, or severity.
metrics.coaching_hint: Characterize the pain: 'Where exactly is the pressure, and when did it start?'

metrics.name: Associated symptoms and risk
metrics.rationale: Checks associated symptoms, history, medications, or risk factors.
metrics.coaching_hint: Ask about associated symptoms and risk factors: 'Are you short of breath, and do you have any heart or blood-pressure history?'

metrics.name: Safety escalation
metrics.rationale: Recognizes the need for urgent escalation in a concerning presentation.
metrics.coaching_hint: Address urgency: 'Given the chest pressure, should we call 911 or arrange an ECG right now?'

metrics.name: Shared next-step confirmation
metrics.rationale: Checks understanding and confirms the immediate next step.
metrics.coaching_hint: Confirm the plan and check understanding: 'Do you have any questions about what happens next?'
